thread:
sam: Heads-up — planned maintenance for the inference runtime node-pool in us-west-2 tonight 23:00–00:30 UTC. Goal: kernel + rollout for better kv-cache handling. Need a short statuspage blurb + an email snippet for affected customers. Can @jordan own customer comms and @ana publish the status page?

deploy-bot: (scheduled) node-pool-update-usw2 scheduled to start 2025-04-15T23:00:00Z — maintenance window 90m. ETA: 23:00 UTC.

ana: I can publish the status page update. Quick question: any customers with pinned model-versions in that pool who need a manual advisory? @luis?

luis: We have 4 Dedicated tenants pinned to xgpt-large:v2 in us-west-2. Routing policy is set to fallback-to-v2-quant with reduced throughput; recommend adding "possible degraded throughput" note and a contact line for SLA-sensitive accounts.

jordan: Ok I’ll draft both. Keeping it short: statuspage: one-line impact, window, expected behavior (automatic routing/fallback), contact link. Email snippet: explicit note about pinned versions + instructions to open a ticket if they need a reserved slot during the window. Drafting now — pasting below.

miriam: FYI I pinged our top-10 watchlist customers and prepped account managers to monitor. They want the support email template so they can forward if needed.

deploy-bot: (info) canary: rollout started on 3/30 nodes in usw2-canary. Monitor tags: latency_p95, tokenization_errors, kv_cache_misses.

ana: Status page copy (ready to publish):
```
Scheduled maintenance — us-west-2 inference runtime
Time: 2025-04-15 23:00 – 2025-04-16 00:30 UTC
Impact: Rolling restarts for runtime optimization. Most requests will be served normally; some requests may see reduced throughput or slightly higher latency. Customers with pinned model versions may experience temporary degraded throughput; automated fallback to compatible quantized variants will occur when necessary.
What we’re doing: kernel and routing updates to improve cache performance and reduce per-token compute.
Contact: https://redwood.example.com/support — for priority customers use the "Escalate" button.
```

jordan: Email snippet for customers:
```
Subject: Planned maintenance for inference runtime in US-WEST-2 (Apr 15)
Hi <Customer>,
We’re performing a planned update to the inference runtime in us-west-2 on Apr 15 23:00–00:30 UTC. The update will improve caching and reduce cost per token long-term. During the window you may see reduced throughput and short-lived higher latency. If you have pinned model versions, our system will attempt automatic fallback to compatible variants; if you require guaranteed capacity please reply and we’ll arrange a reserved slot.
Reported issues? Open a ticket: https://redwood.example.com/support — include "us-west-2 maintenance" in subject.
Regards,
Redwood Support
```

luis: +1 on both. Operational note: if tokenization_errors > 1% sustained for 5m we should pause and rollback kernel. I propose this rollback plan: 1) pause rollout 2) revert kernel 3) re-schedule window for follow-up with knob adjustments. Is that good?

sam: yes agree. Jordan: send the email if we hit rollback trigger. Ana: publish the scheduled status now (status = "scheduled").

deploy-bot: (alert) rollback executed on node-pool-update-usw2 at 2025-04-15T23:18:12Z — reason: tokenization_errors spike 2.4% over 5m. Canary nodes reverted to previous kernel. Notifying watchers.

status-bot: Statuspage updated to: "maintenance in progress — partial rollback occurred; we are investigating. Some customers may experience degraded throughput."

jordan: Sent statuspage incident update and queued the customer email to watchlist. I also cc'd the account managers for pinned customers. Will post a short postmortem stub after we stabilize.

miriam: Thanks — I updated the top-10 with the rollback note and told them to escalate if they see sustained impact.

sam: Good work team. Keep this thread for the public-facing timeline and final follow-up.
